aiTeasers.p: Whether assistants name your store when a local shopper asks.
Drafted responses and summaries so nobody waits on a callback.
More model and service pages, still written in your store’s voice.

aiShifts.p: A chunk of research now happens inside an assistant. Instead of ten blue links, the shopper gets a short answer with two or three stores named. You either appear in it or you don’t exist for that question.
aiShifts.action: Fix: make your site and profile answer real shopper questions plainly.

aiShifts.p: Assistants summarise sentiment across your reviews, not just the star average. A pattern of complaints about the same thing shows up in the answer as a warning, in plain English.
aiShifts.action: Fix: treat review responses as public record, because now they are.

aiShifts.h: Response speed is now table stakes
aiShifts.p: Shoppers who used a chat assistant to research expect a reply in minutes, not by tomorrow morning. AI can draft the reply and summarise the lead, but somebody at the store still has to hit send.
aiShifts.action: Fix: use AI for the first draft, keep a human on the send.

aiShifts.h: Content cost dropped, the bar went up
aiShifts.p: Everyone can now produce model comparison pages in bulk, which means generic pages are worthless. What still works is specifics: your inventory, your market, your pricing, your people.
aiShifts.action: Fix: publish what only your store can say.

aiYes: Drafting first replies to leads for a human to check and send
Summarising long email and chat threads before a callback
Turning one walk-around video into posts, captions and a page
Writing service and model FAQ content from real questions
Spotting patterns across reviews and CRM notes
Cleaning and tagging inventory and photo data
aiNo: Negotiating price or payment with a live shopper
Answering an upset customer’s review unsupervised
Making trade appraisal calls without eyes on the vehicle
Publishing anything about your store nobody has read
Handling a service complaint that should get a phone call
Anything where being wrong costs you the relationship

aiRoadmap.p: Hours, departments, staff, brands, service offerings and inventory structured properly on your own site. Assistants can only repeat what they can parse.
One clear page per question shoppers actually ask — financing, trade, warranty, service intervals, model comparisons in your market.
AI-drafted replies with human approval, measured on minutes-to-first-contact. This is where most stores gain the fastest.
Assistant referrals get reported like any other source, and stores start optimising for them the way they did for search a decade ago.

aeoSteps.p: Clean structured data, complete Google Business Profile, consistent details everywhere. If the basic facts conflict, assistants hedge or skip you.
Short, direct answers on your own pages — the kind an assistant can lift a sentence from. Marketing fluff never gets quoted.
Volume and recency of good reviews, real staff pages, real photos, plus mentions on local sites the assistants already trust.

aiPrompts: Best dealership to buy a used SUV in {your city}?
Which {brand} dealer near {your city} has the best service reputation?
Is {your dealership} a good place to buy a car?
Where can I get a {model} serviced in {your city}?
Which dealer near me is best for first-time buyers with no credit?

aeoWork.p: I run a set of real shopper prompts across the major assistants and record exactly what they say about your store today.
Dealer, department, service and vehicle markup so machines read your site the way a person would.
A batch of plain-language pages covering the questions shoppers actually ask in your market.
Consistent details across Google, directories and local listings so nothing contradicts.
A steady request process plus response coaching, because sentiment feeds directly into AI answers.
Same prompts, re-run, so you can see movement instead of taking my word for it.

aiFaqs.q: Is this just SEO with a new name?
aiFaqs.a: It overlaps a lot. Clean structure, good content, strong reviews help both. The difference is what you optimise for: being the sentence an assistant repeats, not the tenth link on a page.

aiFaqs.q: Should we put an AI chatbot on the website?
aiFaqs.a: Only if someone is watching it. A bot that books appointments and hands off cleanly is useful. One that invents a payment or ignores a question costs you the lead and the trust.

aiFaqs.q: Will AI write all our content now?
aiFaqs.a: It writes drafts. I still edit everything, and the specifics — your inventory, your market, your people — have to come from your store. Generic AI content ranks and converts about as well as it deserves to.

aiFaqs.q: Can you prove any of this moved?
aiFaqs.a: I baseline the same prompts before and after, and track calls, form fills and appointments the way we always have. If a change doesn’t move something you can count, I’ll say so.

timeline.p: Retail sales. Walk-ins, phone ups, month-end. Learned that the deal is won long before anybody talks numbers.
Dealership operations — inventory, process, staffing, the CRM nobody wanted to use. Saw where leads actually die.
Started fixing the marketing side because the marketing side kept sending the store the wrong people.
One person running search, profile, social, email, reviews and follow-up for a short list of dealers.

markets.p: Halifax, Dartmouth, Truro, Sydney, Moncton, Saint John, Fredericton, Charlottetown, St. John’s — home ground.
Ontario, Quebec and the West. Provincial ad rules differ; the process doesn’t.
Single rooftops and small groups. Same channels, different compliance and a much noisier local pack.
Video calls, shared reporting, and a phone number you can actually reach during your hours.

emailStats.p: No platform between you and the customer, and nobody can raise the price of reaching them.
A past customer costs a fraction of a third-party lead and closes at a far better rate.
Your service lane sees equity customers twice a year. Email is how you get in front of them between visits.
Opens are noise now. I report replies, appointments booked and units delivered.

emailSends.p: Customers in a payment position to upgrade, matched to units you actually have.
Timed to the vehicle, not the calendar, with a booking link that works on a phone.
Ninety, sixty and thirty days out, before the other store gets there first.
Three touches in the first month — this is where reviews and referrals come from.
Customers who haven’t been in for eighteen months and think you forgot them.

personal.v: Nova Scotia, working with stores across Canada and the US — on the phone during your hours, not mine.
Deliberately small. I turn down work rather than hand it to someone you’ve never met.
Month to month. If I’m not earning it, you shouldn’t be locked in.
Calls, forms, appointments. Not impressions and reach.
Canadian. Your shoppers notice when the copy sounds American.
